description: Static benchmark pack for customer support automation (spec 4.1). Loaded at request time; no live calls. NOTE: this sector is materially less well sourced than document_processing — see pack_health in lib/benchmarks.py.

figures.label: Customer service representatives — median hourly wage
figures.source: US Bureau of Labor Statistics, Occupational Employment and Wage Statistics (OEWS), SOC 43-4051
figures.notes: BASE wage only — not fully loaded. bls.gov blocks automated retrieval (HTTP 403), so this was read from a search result attributed to BLS rather than the page itself; re-verify before publishing a report that cites it.

figures.label: Fully-loaded cost multiplier over base wage
figures.source: assumption — no primary source located for a defensible loading factor
figures.notes: Covers employer taxes, benefits, facilities and overhead. Explicitly an assumption.

figures.label: Additional tickets per hour handled by AI-assisted agents
figures.notes: Vendor-published research; the vendor sells the automation being measured, so treat as directionally useful rather than independent. Retrieved via a search result, not the report itself.
figures.population: 5,179 customer-support agents in one vendor-published study
figures.applicability: supports an AI-ASSISTED PRODUCTIVITY scenario only
figures.limitations: a productivity uplift is NOT an automation rate and NOT a headcount reduction; vendor-published, and the vendor sells the automation being measured

figures.label: Fully-loaded cost per support ticket, North America
figures.source: commonly cited as HDI / Gartner cost-per-ticket benchmarks, but only reachable through secondary industry summaries; primary report not retrieved
figures.notes: Recorded as ASSUMED, not sourced, precisely because the chain of custody stops at aggregator blogs. Spec 4.3 forbids laundering an industry average into something that reads as company-specific or independently sourced. Replace with the HDI/Gartner primary before this figure appears in a report.

figures.label: Fully-loaded cost per support contact, global baseline
figures.source: secondary industry summaries; primary report not retrieved
figures.notes: Wide dispersion by channel and industry (self-service $1-4, phone $17-25 per the same secondary sources). Low decision value until sourced properly.

figures.label: Average handling time per ticket
figures.notes: Spec 4.1 names this a ground-truth figure for the sector, but no primary source was located. The interviewer asks for this field directly (it is not benchmark_substitutable), so this default should rarely be needed.

figures.label: Tickets handled per agent per day
figures.notes: Useful only as a sanity check against volume / headcount / handling time supplied by the user.

figures.label: Share of a support agent's time spent on ticket handling
figures.notes: The interviewer treats this field as benchmark_substitutable and will not ask for it, so this assumed default is what the analysis will use unless the user overrides at review (spec 6, 10.5).
